title: How to brief a workwear manufacturer for a whole team
description: Plan branded workwear around job roles, movement, laundering and replacement orders. Test a pilot garment with the people who will actually wear it.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: Start a workwear order by listing what each team member does during a normal shift. A reception employee, a stockroom colleague and a mobile supervisor may share one brand identity while needing different layers, pocket positions and fits. A useful uniform brief makes those differences visible before anyone approves a company-wide order.

toc.text: Watch a task before choosing a garment
Agree how the uniform will be cared for
How do you keep staff reorders consistent when employees join at different times?
Design the reorder while choosing the first run

bodyHtml:
Watch a task before choosing a garment

In a furniture showroom, staff might welcome visitors, carry fabric books and kneel to demonstrate a storage unit. Ask a representative wearer to perform those actions in the sample. A logo can sit well in a standing photo and vanish under a radio strap. A pen pocket can be easy to reach while standing and awkward at a desk. Write observations in terms of tasks so the pattern maker can reproduce the problem.

Build a role sheet

RoleGarment requirement to testTrial question
Front of houseComfortable layer and consistent logo visibilityCan customers recognise the team with the outer layer open?
StockroomReach, pocket access and easy changingCan staff work through a normal set of movements?
Mobile supervisorLayering over a shirt and access to a notebookDo the pockets still work when the vest is closed?

This is a brief for ordinary branded work clothing. If a role requires protective performance, identify the hazard with the responsible safety professional and specify the corresponding evidence for that product before procurement. A branded vest or bright colour alone establishes no protective rating. EU guidance on workplace PPE

Agree how the uniform will be cared for

Ask whether garments will be washed at home or through a laundry service. Give the supplier the intended care routine and agree what the sample trial should examine. Check fit after care, logo appearance and whether a badge or trim rubs during a shift. Record the trial conditions so a future change in care can be recognised.

How do you keep staff reorders consistent when employees join at different times?

Keep one reference sheet per role, with a style code, colour reference, approved decoration and person responsible for changes. If the uniform is updated, date the change and tell the issuing team which version can be handed out alongside the old one. A role name such as “front desk” alone will not identify the correct garment.

Design the reorder while choosing the first run

Record role, style code, colour standard, size and branding file. Decide who can request replacements and how new employees will choose a size. Keep an approved sample for comparison, especially if branches will place orders independently. Separate an adjustment for one role from a global change to the whole uniform.

Discuss branded workwear with BEWE4R. Include the job roles, work setting, size range and the task your pilot garment must pass.
